title: 第一卷 第17章 李群书高光时刻第一卷 第18章 杂役殿殿主苍古仙人收徒李群书
content_zh:
林罪推开破屋的门，李群书正盘腿坐在床上。
听到脚步声，他睁开眼，看到是林罪，激动的从床上蹦下来。
“罪哥！合气丹真牛，一颗就让我体内诞生了一丝仙力。”
他伸出两根手指，比了个很小的缝隙，“就这么一丝，但我感觉到，照这个进度，我最多最多，只需要一百颗合气丹，我就能破凡成仙，成为一骨人仙！”
林罪微微一愣。
一百颗。
同样是合气丹，他的《噬经》百分百吸收能量，没有造成一丝能量浪费，两颗下去才淬炼了整块仙骨的百分之一。
也就是说，他需要两百颗。
而李群书修炼的是《长生经》，却只需要一百颗。
怎么感觉哪里不对？
而且按照长生经的修炼效率，一颗合气丹的吸收率只有六七成，就能让李群书完成百分之一的进度。
是他的仙骨更能吃，还是其它原因？
林罪看向李群书，笑了笑。
“走，给我展示一下。”
……
两人随后去到院子里。
李群书走到院子废弃的石磨旁边，那一块石头，少说也得有三四百斤的重量。
“罪哥，看好了。”
李群书挽起袖子，手臂青筋暴起，略带费力的将石磨盘起。
坚持了十秒后，脸红脖子粗的将石磨扔到地上。

“呼～，罪哥，厉害吧！”
林罪对他竖起了大拇指，“你刚才用了多大的力气？”
“大概用了八成。”
林罪若有所思，他大致明白了，他的仙骨大概率和别人不一样。
吃得多，但力量增加得也多。
同样淬炼百分之一，他的“百分之一”和李群书的“百分之一”不一样。
李群书甩了甩手臂。
“罪哥，你说这是不是就是仙凡之别？体内有仙力的人和没有的人，完全就是两个世界的，连一块仙骨都没淬炼完，就已经这样了，那要是修成一骨人仙……”
他没有继续说下去，但眼睛里浮现一种笃定的神色。
林罪看着他，想起几天前在竹林里第一次见到他的情景。
那时候李群书蹲在地上扒竹笋，对修仙这件事本身的憧憬，像是小孩子看到糖葫芦一样。
现在，他已经尝到了修行的甜头，尝过了拥有力量带来的改变。
不知道日后，还能不能保持那颗赤子之心。
……
后半夜，林罪发现。
李群书失眠了，他躺在床上，眼睛还是睁着的，盯着破了个洞的屋顶，像是在看什么地方。
林罪缓缓闭上眼睛，李群书有机缘，否则，一个一骨雏形，不会进步那么快。
而且李群书说过，他家祖上出过六骨人仙。
content_en:
Lin Zui pushed open the door of the broken house and saw Li Qunshu sitting cross-legged on the bed.
Hearing footsteps, he opened his eyes and saw that it was Lin Zui, and jumped out of bed excitedly.
"Brother Zui! The Heqi Pill is so awesome. One pill gave birth to a trace of immortal power in my body."
He stretched out two fingers and made a small gap, "It's just a small gap, but I feel that according to this progress, at most, I only need a hundred Heqi Pills, and I can break through the mortal world and become an immortal, becoming a one-bone human immortal!"
Lin Zui was slightly startled.
One hundred.
It is also a combination of Qi pills. His "Eating Sutra" absorbs 100% of the energy without causing any waste of energy. Only two pills can temper one percent of the entire immortal bone.
In other words, he needs two hundred.
But Li Qunshu was practicing the "Sutra of Immortality", but he only needed a hundred pills.
Why do you feel something is wrong?
Moreover, according to the cultivation efficiency of the Immortal Sutra, the absorption rate of a Heqi Pill is only 60-70%, which can allow Li Qunshu to complete 1% of the progress.
Is it because his immortal bones are more edible, or is it for other reasons?
Lin Zui looked at Li Qunshu and smiled.
"Come on, show me."
…
The two then went to the yard.
Li Qunshu walked to the abandoned stone mill in the yard. The stone weighed at least three to four hundred kilograms.
"Brother Zui, watch carefully."
Li Qunshu rolled up his sleeves, veins popped up in his arms, and he lifted the stone mill with a little effort.
After holding on for ten seconds, he threw the stone mill to the ground with a blushing face.
"Hoo~, Brother Zui, you are so awesome!"
Lin Zui gave him a thumbs up, "How much strength did you use just now?"
"About 80% of it is used."
Lin Zui was thoughtful, and he roughly understood that his immortal bones were most likely different from others.
The more you eat, the more your strength increases.
Also tempering one percent, his "one percent" is different from Li Qunshu's "one percent".
Li Qunshu shook his arm.
"Brother Zui, do you think this is the difference between immortals and mortals? Those who have immortal power in their bodies and those who don't are in two completely different worlds. They haven't even finished tempering a single immortal bone. That's already the case. Then if you become a human immortal with one bone..."
He did not continue, but there was a look of determination in his eyes.
Lin Zui looked at him and remembered the first time he saw him in the bamboo forest a few days ago.
At that time, Li Qunshu was squatting on the ground picking bamboo shoots, and his longing for the matter of cultivating immortals was like a child seeing a candied haws.
Now, he has tasted the sweetness of practice and the changes brought about by having power.
I don’t know if I can maintain that innocent heart in the future.
…
Later in the night, Lin Zui found out.
Li Qunshu had insomnia. He was lying on the bed, his eyes still open, staring at the hole in the roof, as if he was looking somewhere.
Lin Zui slowly closed his eyes. Li Qunshu had a chance, otherwise, a one-bone prototype would not have progressed so fast.
Moreover, Li Qunshu said that his ancestors had six-bone immortals.
